sense: an owner; the one in charge of a house, an animal, a slave

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.139: nec domō dominus, sed dominō domus honestanda est
terms.comment: The owner of a house, an estate, a slave or an animal, and so a lord and ruler; a woman is domina. In Christian Latin Dominus is the Lord; in address it is polite, “sir” (Lewis & Short). For the boss who employs one, see employer.

evidence: Plaut. Am. 141, Trin. 2.4.34; Cic. Off. 2.24 (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The master of the household as his slaves speak of him; the mistress is era. Chiefly in comedy, where the slaves’ erus major and erus minor are the old and the young master (Plaut. As. 2.2.63, Lewis & Short). Lewis & Short prefers the spelling without h.
The one who holds property, especially land; in post-Augustan law also the defendant who holds what is claimed (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: nec domō dominus, sed dominō domus honestanda est
phrases.english: the master should not be honoured by his house, but the house by its master

sources: Lewis & Short: dominus · Lewis & Short: erus · Lewis & Short: possessor
